duration_exposure_text.description: Length of time between start of exposure and outcome assessment, in days when <7 (e.g., 5d), weeks when ≥7 days to 12 weeks (e.g., 1wk, 12wk), or months when >12 weeks (e.g., 15mon). lifestage_exposed.description: Definitions: Developmental: Prenatal and perinatal exposure in dams or postnatal exposure in offspring until sexual maturity (~6 weeks in rats and mice). Include studies with pre-mating exposure if the endpoint focus is developmental. Juvenile: Exposure between weaned and sexual maturity. Adult: Exposure in sexually mature males or females. Adult (gestation): Exposure in dams duringpregnancy. Multi-lifestage: includes both developmental and adult (i.e., multi-generational studies, exposure that start before sexual maturity and continue to adulthood)

lifestage_assessed.description: Definitions: Developmental: Prenatal and perinatal exposure in dams or postnatal exposure in offspring until sexual maturity (~6 weeks in rats and mice). comments.description: Copy paste animal husbandry information from materials and methods, use quotation marks around all text directly copy/pasted from paper.

diet.description: Describe diet as presented in the paper (e.g., "soy-protein free 2020X Teklad," "Atromin 1310", "standard rodent chow").

strain.description: When adding a new strain, put the stock in parenthesis, e.g., "Sprague-Dawley (Harlan)."

slug.description: The URL (web address) used to describe this object (no spaces or special-characters).

significance_level.description: Enter statistical significance level for the effect. Typically this is as presented in the study. Indicate in the results comment field if it is based on statistical analysis conducted by the assessment team

treatment_effect.description: Expert judgement based report of treatment related effects (add direction if known). Use when statistical analysis not available. In results comments, indicate whether it was author judgment or assessment team judgement

litter_effects.description: Type of controls used for litter-effects. The "No" response will be infrequently used. More typically the information will be "Not reported" and assumed not considered. Only use "No" if it is explicitly mentioned in the study that litter was not controlled for.

litter_effect_notes.description: Any additional notes describing how litter effects were controlled

observation_time.description: Numeric value of the time an observation was reported; optional, should be recorded if the same effect was measured multiple times.

observation_time_text.description: Text for reported observation time (ex: "60-90 PND")

data_location.description: Details on where the data are found in the literature (ex: "Figure 1", "Table 2", "Text, p. 24", "Figure 1 and Text, p.24")

expected_adversity_direction.description: Response direction which would be considered adverse

response_units.description: Units the response was measured in (i.e., μg/dL, % control, etc.)

data_reported.description: Dose-response data for endpoint are available in the literature source

data_extracted.description: Dose-response data for endpoint are extracted from literature into HAWC

values_estimated.description: Response values were estimated using a digital ruler or other methods

statistical_test.description: Short description of statistical analysis techniques used, e.g., Fisher Exact Test, ANOVA, Chi Square, Peto's test, none conducted

trend_value.description: Numerical result for trend-test, if available

diagnostic.description: List the endpoint/adverse outcome name as used in the study. This will help during QA/QC of the extraction to the original study in cases where the endpoint/adverse outcome name is adjusted for consistency across studies or assessments.

power_notes.description: Power of study-design to detect change from control

results_notes.description: Qualitative description of the results. This field can be left blank if there is no need to further describe numerically extracted findings, e.g., organ or body weights. Use this field to describe findings such as the type and severity of histopathology or malformations not otherwise captured in the numerical data extraction. Also use this field to cut and paste findings described only in text in the study. If coding is used to create exposure-response arrays, then add this comment in bold font at the start of the text box entry "For exposure-response array data display purposes, the following results were coded (control and no effect findings were coded as "0", treatment-related increases were coded as "1", and treatment-related decreases were coded as "-1"."

endpoint_notes.description: Cut and paste from methods, use quotation marks around all text directly copy/pasted from paper. editable.description: Project-managers and team-members are allowed to edit this study.
